findings.title: Reasoning-agent unset-fallback undocumented after pin to DEFAULT_MODEL value
findings.evidence:
tenant_scorer/.env.example:10-15
# (defaults to DEFAULT_MODEL when unset; pinned to gemini-3.6-flash in terraform)
COMPLIANCE_REPAIR_MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash

# All reasoning agents on gemini-3.6-flash (cost optimization: 3.6 Flash
# benchmarks higher than 3.1 Pro on intelligence, price, and speed).
CONSISTENCY_CHECKER_MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash
findings.detail: Reasoning agents now equal DEFAULT_MODEL, yet only COMPLIANCE_REPAIR documents its unset fallback. A deployer who unsets the reasoning vars cannot tell from .env.example whether they fall back to DEFAULT_MODEL or to a pro model.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a "defaults to DEFAULT_MODEL when unset" note (or state the real fallback) to the reasoning-agent block so unset behavior is explicit.

findings.title: Cost-optimization rationale rests on an uncited benchmark claim
findings.evidence:
tenant_scorer/.env.example:13-14
# All reasoning agents on gemini-3.6-flash (cost optimization: 3.6 Flash
# benchmarks higher than 3.1 Pro on intelligence, price, and speed).
findings.detail: The comment asserts 3.6 Flash beats 3.1 Pro on intelligence, price, and speed with no source. If the intelligence claim is false, reasoning quality on the checker, compliance judge, and final reviewer regresses. (Briefing documents the Artificial Analysis verification separately; the code comment itself is uncited.)
findings.recommended_fix: Cite the benchmark source in the comment or drop the intelligence claim, retaining only the verifiable cost reduction, so the rationale is auditable.

findings.title: 3 of 5 Pro agents lack the per-agent model assertion their siblings have
findings.evidence:
tests/unit/test_agents_consistency_checker.py:29:        assert agent.model.model == "gemini-3.6-flash"
tests/unit/test_agents_risk_scorer.py:39:        assert agent.model.model == "gemini-3.6-flash"
tenant_scorer/agents/verification_compliance_judge.py:216:        model=get_agent_llm("verification_compliance_judge"),
tenant_scorer/agents/final_compliance_reviewer.py:234:        model=get_agent_llm("final_compliance_reviewer"),
tenant_scorer/agents/personal_statement_analyzer.py:309:        model=get_agent_llm("personal_statement_analyzer"),
tests/unit/test_config.py:66-73: test_all_agents_default_to_gemini_flash asserts every agent resolves to gemini-3.6-flash
findings.detail: Diff moves 5 Pro agents to flash. consistency_checker and risk_scorer unit tests assert agent.model.model == 'gemini-3.6-flash'; the other 3 omit it, so an agent-wiring regression there is caught only by the function-level test, not the constructed object.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a test_model() asserting agent.model.model == 'gemini-3.6-flash' to the verification_compliance_judge, final_compliance_reviewer and personal_statement_analyzer unit tests, matching their 2 siblings.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: PASS
findings.detail: Config-value-only diff (Terraform/env/README + a config.py comment). Runtime resolution fully covered: all 12 agents resolve to gemini-3.6-flash, fallback chain, dedup/tag-suffix. P0 n/a; P1 resolution 100%; overall >=80%.
findings.recommended_fix: None required to pass. Optional defence-in-depth: add the 3 missing per-agent model assertions noted above. Terraform/env values rely on terraform tooling, not pytest (by design).
